foil.title: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption state
foil.scenario_short: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption stands at 73% over 30 days, with 78% pressure and 79% state confirmation feeding energy supply shock, reinforced by 7 urgent critical signals and headlines about...
foil.perspective_strategic: Red Sea maritime disruption state with 78% pressure and 79% state confirmation, combined with 7 urgent critical signals, indicates strong energy repricing pressure, but the single clustered situation and single linked forecast suggest narrow transmission pathways.
foil.perspective_contrarian: Counter-evidence includes U.S. crude oil falls below $95 per barrel as market hopes for diplomatic resolution to Iran war, suggesting diplomatic progress could reduce energy repricing pressure despite the 78% state confirmation.
foil.actor_lens: Commodity traders: Price whether stress in Red Sea becomes durable over the 30d. Rebalance positions if the probability path moves away from 73%.
foil.top_signal: Red Sea maritime disruption state is feeding energy repricing through energy supply shock, with 78% pressure and 79% state confirmation

This is the honest inverse: for an observed natural-hazard fact, the sourced record IS the only trustworthy source.
